quote: The experimental evidence for a purely genetic component of 0.6–0.8 is overwhelming
content: Twin and adoption studies do put the heritability of adult IQ in roughly the 0.5-0.8 range, so the number is not invented, but "a purely genetic component" misstates what heritability is. Heritability is a population statistic, the share of trait variance attributable to genetic differences in a particular population and environment, not a fixed property of the trait, and it shifts with circumstances: Turkheimer et al. (2003) found IQ heritability near zero in impoverished children and high in affluent ones. Heritability of IQ also rises with age, and molecular genetics has so far recovered only a fraction of the twin-study estimate (the "missing heritability" problem). "Overwhelming" and "purely genetic" overstate a real but heavily conditional finding.
